To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

muon pair production by high energy muon and muon bundle is a significant contribution to the flux of muon bundles underground, but the cross section for muon pair production is much smaller than that used in previous studies.
muon pair production by high energy muon and muon bundles underground is an important source of muon pairs in underground experiments.

muon pair production by high energy muon is a significant source of muon bundles underground; the contribution of this process to the intensity of double and triple events underground is comparable to that of muon bremsstrahlung; the ratio of the intensity of double muon events to that of single muon events is about 1/2000 at 1kmW.E.; and the intensity of triple muon events is less than 1/100 of the intensity of single muon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of muon pairs and bundles produced by high-energy muons in rock and in water.
the study of muon pair and triplet production in the rock.
the development of a method for calculating the cross section of muon pair formation in electromagnetic interactions of high-energy muons with nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the muon pair production by muons underground does not significantly contribute to the observed narrow muon bundles.
the muon pair production by muons is a negligible process for the muon bundles observed underground.

the cross sections for muon pair production by high energy muon beams and muon bundles have been calculated and that the contribution of the process to the observed muon flux underground has been evaluated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
muon bundles are produced mainly by muons and muon pairs, and the contribution of muons to the intensity of muon bundles underground is about 50% for depths of 1 km.
muon pair production can be neglected in calculations of the muon intensity underground.
muon pair production by single muons is negligible for muon bundles underground, and the observed flux of narrow muon events can be explained by a single muon mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
muon pair production by high energy muon is not an important mechanism to produce narrow muon bundles in rock.
the contribution of the electromagnetic production of muons to the muon flux underground is negligible.
muon pairs produced in electromagnetic interactions are much more rare than it has been assumed in the literature.
